questions.question: What does the "masters lunch" theme actually mean for this 30th — should your menu play to it?

options.label: The Masters (golf)
options.description: Augusta clubhouse vibe — pimento cheese, Southern US classics, green jackets. I'll work the theme in.

options.label: Academic "masters"
options.description: Clever, refined, graduation-grade — no literal food theme, just an impressive menu.

options.label: No theme, dream menu
options.description: Forget the theme — just send my genuine ideal 3 courses, themed or not.

options.label: Long boozy lunch
options.description: "Masters" = a masterclass long lunch. Lean into a slow, indulgent, wine-led sitting.

questions.question: What overall feel do you want your three courses to have?

options.label: Comfort, done perfectly
options.description: The best version of obvious crowd-pleasers. No reinvention, all execution.

options.label: Fresh and bright
options.description: Seafood-forward, acidic, lighter — built for a sunny lunch.

options.label: Indulgent and rich
options.description: Big flavours, fat, char, butter. Unapologetic.

options.label: Adventurous / chef-y
options.description: Surprising techniques and combinations — show off a bit.

questions.question: What should anchor your main course?

options.label: Red meat
options.description: Steak, lamb, or similar — coal-fired and serious.

options.label: Seafood
options.description: Fish, shellfish, or a whole-fish centrepiece.

options.label: Poultry / pork
options.description: Roast chook, duck, or slow pork.

options.label: Surprise me
options.description: Pick whatever makes the strongest menu.
